Continuation tied to Astra corpus revision

STATUS AND SCOPE

This note replaces the earlier clamp/marked-null observation contract for ONE
explicit known architecture. It derives the missing inputs from one ordinary
native trajectory. The observation is an initial state followed by every actual
state change and its timestamp. There are no clamp interventions, channel
labels, attempted-update marks, null-event marks, or stationary initial samples.

The statistical engine is conventional continuous-time Markov-chain likelihood
and counting-process concentration. The useful architecture-specific algebra
is an explicit selection of unmixed local intensities. This is not a claim to
have invented a new likelihood estimator. Correctly informed ordinary methods
already supply this acquisition step. The surviving research contribution must
therefore lie in the downstream rare-event transfer mechanism and its scope,
not in presenting count/exposure estimation as new.

The source is assumed to be exactly in the architecture below. The selected
data do NOT certify arbitrary additional channels, state-dependent rare gates,
or a generally misspecified native generator. Applying a general perturbation
certificate would require acquiring all local aggregate-rate boxes that its
hypotheses demand. That has not been done in the accompanying fixture.

1. NATIVE GENERATOR AND OBSERVATION CONTRACT

Use zero-based sites i=0,...,n-1. The unknown factors obey

    9/10 <= a_i,b_i <= 11/10,   1/2 <= alpha_i <= 1,

and the unnormalized stationary weight is

    w(x) = product_i a_i^(x_i) product_i b_i^(x_i x_(i+1)),
    x in {0,1}^n,   pi(x)=w(x)/Z.

There is a known unit-rate heatbath contribution at every site. Its conditional
odds and actual single-bit transition rates are

    r_i(l,r)=a_i b_(i-1)^l b_i^r,
    q_i(0->1)=r_i/(1+r_i),   q_i(1->0)=1/(1+r_i),

with absent boundary factors omitted. The rate one is an independently known
time scale. It is not estimated from invisible nulls.

On adjacent sites i,i+1 let

    v_i(u,v;l,r)=a_i^u a_(i+1)^v
                b_(i-1)^(l u) b_i^(u v) b_(i+1)^(v r).

    00 -> 10 -> 11 -> 00,

and odd i has the reverse cycle

PASSIVE NATIVE-HISTORY IMPLEMENTATION REVIEW

FILES REVIEWED

passive_native.cpp
analyze_passive.py
passive_native_history.json
passive_results.json

INTERFACE BOUNDARY

NativeSource alone owns a,b,alpha, hidden proposal choices, acceptance draws,
and nulls. PassiveObserver is constructed with n, integer R and the initial
state. Its on_change callback has only the new full state and timestamp.
No proposal label, accepted-channel identifier or null callback is supplied.
The observer uses actual changed support to distinguish single and double
jumps. Two different native channels that share a one-bit destination are
therefore aggregated, as required by the observation model.

The source is simulated by uniformization at rate 3n-2. Hidden proposals are
counted separately as computational simulation work; they are not treated as
observed statistical samples. The driver invokes the observer's own quota
timers before the next native proposal when necessary. Such a timer is entirely
determined by prior observed state changes and accumulated exposure. It reveals
no hidden source event: continuous observation already says that the currently
observed state has not changed before that timer.

EXPOSURE AND COUNT ORDERING

Each context stores its completed occupation and, when active, the beginning
of its current active sojourn. Its deadline is start+(R-exposure). A set of at
most m deadlines is updated whenever an actual change affects that context.
Thus there is no accumulation of stale per-event timers.

At an actual change time the observer first completes all quota deadlines
already reached, then counts the jump only in a still active, unfinished
context, then updates contexts under the new state. This implements freezing
N_c at occupation time R. Events at exactly a real quota boundary have
probability zero in the ideal model; the code's deterministic tie convention
processes quota completion first. Different contexts can complete at different
times, and an already completed context never acquires additional counts.

For single-bit changes at i the context index is 2i+right, with the absent
right bit treated as zero. This agrees with the final site's single context.
